evals.prompt: Here is the epic PRD at docs/ways-of-work/plan/usage-based-billing/epic.md. Produce the architecture spec for it.
evals.expected_output: An architecture specification saved to docs/ways-of-work/plan/usage-based-billing/arch.md with a layered Mermaid diagram, features, enablers, stack, technical value and t-shirt size.
expectations: The document contains a Mermaid diagram with subgraphs for user, application, service, data and infrastructure layers
The document lists High-Level Features and Technical Enablers as separate lists
The document gives a T-Shirt Size Estimate (S, M, L or XL)
The document contains no implementation code other than pseudocode

evals.prompt: Create the architecture document for the notifications epic in web-app.
evals.expected_output: The agent looks for docs/ways-of-work/plan/notifications/epic.md and, when it does not exist, asks for the Epic PRD instead of inventing requirements.
expectations: The agent reads or searches for the Epic PRD before writing
When no Epic PRD exists the agent asks for it or for its content rather than writing arch.md from guesses
No arch.md is written whose features are unrelated to any stated requirement

evals.prompt: Architecture spec for the data-residency epic (PRD in docs/ways-of-work/plan/data-residency/epic.md). We run Python with FastAPI and Django, not TypeScript, and deploy on Kubernetes without Docker Compose.
evals.expected_output: An architecture spec whose Technology Stack and diagram reflect the stated Python and Kubernetes stack rather than the default TypeScript assumptions.
expectations: The Technology Stack section names Python, FastAPI or Django and Kubernetes
The Technology Stack section does not list tRPC or Next.js as the chosen stack
The Technical Value section gives a High, Medium or Low rating with a justification
